name: Canadian pressure pumping oilfield services company (fracturing, cementing, coiled tubing)
modelled_on: Trican Well Service Ltd. (Calgary; main model for scale, service lines, bases, fleet and activity 2019-2022)
STEP Energy Services Ltd., Canadian segment (fracturing and coiled tubing activity, workforce, seasonality)
summary: The company pumps fluids, sand and cement into oil and gas wells for producers in the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin, mainly in Alberta and northeast British Columbia. Its largest service is hydraulic fracturing, which cracks open tight rock along horizontal wells and props the cracks with sand; it also cements steel casing in newly drilled wells and runs coiled tubing units that mill out plugs and clean wells after fracturing. Customers are more than 60 oil and gas producers, a few of which provide a large share of revenue, and the company earns money per job under master service agreements and tendered programs, billing equipment time, crews and materials from signed field tickets. Revenue was about $560-870 million a year in 2019-2022, about three quarters of it from fracturing. The work follows the drilling cycle: it peaks in winter when frozen ground allows access, nearly stops during spring break-up road bans, and swings with commodity prices, which led to deep cuts in 2020 and a hiring scramble in 2021-2022. Field operations run from district bases in Red Deer, Grande Prairie, Whitecourt, Fort St. John and southern Alberta, supported by a sand and chemical supply chain, equipment maintenance and manufacturing shops, a cement and fluids laboratory and a Calgary head office for sales, engineering, finance, HR and HSE.

process_map.name: Respond to producer tenders
process_map.description: An account manager receives a producer's tender for a fracturing program or annual cementing and coiled tubing work, a pricing analyst builds the price from the price book and expected costs, and engineers add designs and equipment plans. Short deadlines, many line items and the need to price sand, fuel and trucking pass-throughs make bids slow and error-prone.

evidence.note: Pricing pressure and long-term pricing work with customers described in src1. Volume tier C: more than 60 customers, most programs rebid yearly or per pad.

surge.cause: Autumn budget season when producers tender the next year's completion programs and annual service contracts

evidence.note: Firm commitments for the next year's fleets were secured in the autumn (worldoil-2018, November 2018); multiplier tier C.

process_map.name: Negotiate master service agreements and pricing
process_map.description: After an award, sales and legal negotiate or renew the master service agreement and the customer-specific pricing schedule, including indemnities, insurance limits and cost escalation clauses. Producers push their own forms, so redlines go back and forth for weeks.

evidence.note: Standard practice for WCSB service contractors; src1 mentions working with customers on long-term pricing and passing on inflation.

surge.cause: Year-end and first-quarter repricing when annual awards and cost escalation take effect

evidence.note: Prices raised for all clients through Q4 2021 and into Q1 2022 (step-2021); multiplier tier C.

process_map.name: Maintain customer price books
process_map.description: Pricing analysts load agreed prices, discounts and pass-through rules for sand, fuel and trucking into the ERP and field ticket app, and update them when costs change. A wrong price book entry flows into every field ticket and invoice until a customer disputes it.

evidence.note: Inflation on operating inputs passed on to clients in 2022 (src8). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Manage customer accounts
process_map.description: Account managers hold regular reviews with producers on safety, efficiency and scorecards, track disputes and overdue invoices, and plan next year's work. Concentration matters: one customer gave 31% of revenue, so a lost relationship changes fleet plans.

evidence.note: More than 60 customers; one customer 31% of revenue in 2021 and 2022. Review volume tier C.

process_map.name: Provide technical support to customers
process_map.description: Technical sales engineers answer producers' questions on designs, fluids, cement blends and coiled tubing reach, run quick models and bring lab or design work into bids. Requests arrive by phone and email at all hours and compete with field support.

evidence.note: Engineering support and technical solutions described (src6, src5). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Take job calls and dispatch crews
process_map.description: Dispatchers take calls from drilling rigs and producers for cementing, coiled tubing and nitrogen jobs, check crew hours, unit availability and materials, and assign a crew with a call-out time. Rig timing changes by the hour, so jobs are rescheduled often and crews wait on location.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.

Volume from ofs-fo-dist-job-call-intake-and-dispatch (2026-11-24): Organisation file splits: about 400 cementing jobs, 50 remedial jobs and 140 coiled tubing and nitrogen jobs a month, plus about 5-8% of calls that are cancelled or declined. The organisation file's driver (all jobs invoiced) also includes about 50 fracturing wells a month that do not come through job calls.

process_map.name: Schedule crews and rotations
process_map.description: District managers and HR coordinators build rotation schedules for each crew, cover sickness and turnover, check tickets and driving hours, and record field time for payroll. Short-staffed crews delay jobs or need overtime.
process_map.unit_of_work: one weekly crew schedule for a service line in a district

evidence.note: Difficulty adding field crews and retaining personnel (src1). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter peak (January to mid-March) when every crew is active and cover is hardest to find

evidence.note: Crews booked through the first quarter and tight supply of field staff (step-2021); multiplier tier C.

process_map.name: Move equipment between pads and bases
process_map.description: Planners and supervisors plan routes and permits for moving a frac fleet of 30 to 50 heavy units, check road bans and lease access, and schedule tractors and drivers. Road bans, weather and lease road conditions decide when a move can start.
process_map.unit_of_work: one fleet move (pad to pad, or base to pad)

surge.cause: Post-break-up restart when road bans lift and fleets move out together

evidence.note: Road bans lift as thaw ends (src12); multiplier tier C.

Volume from ofs-fo-dist-equipment-mobilization (2026-11-24): One move into each pad (about 18 a month) plus occasional base trips for maintenance; slightly below the organisation file's 8-20-30 because pad-corridor work avoids some moves.

process_map.name: Prepare and get field tickets signed
process_map.description: At the end of a job the supervisor enters services, equipment hours and materials into the field ticket app, the customer's wellsite supervisor reviews and signs it, and district administrators check it against the job file and price book. Missing signatures and quantity disputes hold up billing.
process_map.unit_of_work: one field ticket (one cementing job, one coiled tubing or nitrogen day, or one frac pumping day on a pad)

evidence.note: Volume from ofs-fo-dist-field-ticket-preparation (2026-11-24): Jobs are about 7,300-7,600 a year (about 620 a month, trican-mda-2022), and a job is typically one invoice. Tickets outnumber invoices because frac pads and multi-day coiled tubing jobs are ticketed per day and rolled into one invoice per well or pad: about 420 cementing tickets, 200 coiled tubing and nitrogen day tickets and 130 frac day tickets (7 crews x about 18 pumping days) a month. Low end is break-up and 2020.

surge.cause: December program completions, when producers push to finish capital programs and close AFEs before year end

evidence.note: Year-end completion push described in the organisation file's surge for billing; size estimated.

process_map.name: Run base yards and wash bays
process_map.description: Yard operators wash, fuel, stage and park returning equipment, keep the yard safe and log units for inspection. Units returning from muddy leases in spring and fall queue for the wash bay before shop work can start.

evidence.note: Nine bases listed (src3). Volume = bases x days, tier C.

process_map.name: Hold the daily operations call
process_map.description: District and service line managers review yesterday's jobs, tomorrow's schedule, equipment down and crew gaps on a morning call and move units or crews between districts. Decisions rely on whiteboards and spreadsheets updated by each base.

evidence.note: Common practice in multi-district service companies.

process_map.name: Plan a pad fracturing program
process_map.description: Coordinators turn an awarded pad into a plan: fleet and crew dates, horsepower, proppant and chemical volumes, fuel, site layout and the interface with the producer's wireline and water suppliers. Customer schedule changes ripple into sand orders and other pads.
process_map.unit_of_work: one pad program (a multi-well pad of typically two to six horizontal wells)

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
Crews, proppant and customer program changes described (src1, src2). Pads per month tier C (about 3 wells per pad).

process_map.name: Rig up the frac fleet and pressure test
process_map.description: The crew spots pumps, blender, data van and sand units on the pad, connects treating iron to the wellhead, holds the pre-job safety meeting and pressure tests the lines. Rig-up takes most of a day and cannot start until the lease is ready.

evidence.note: Heavy-duty pumps for 24-hour operations (src2). Steps and volume tier C.

process_map.name: Pump fracturing stages
process_map.description: The 24-hour crew pumps each stage to the design while the treater watches pressures from the data van, alternating with the producer's wireline crew that perforates the next stage. Screen-outs, pump failures, sand and fuel shortages and wireline delays stop the work while the whole fleet stands by.
process_map.unit_of_work: one well fractured (all stages of one horizontal well)

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
Crews, proppant and HHP figures (src1); Directive 083 subsurface integrity rules (src9). Wells per month tier C.

process_map.name: Manage proppant and chemicals on location
process_map.description: Sand operators receive truckloads, check load tickets, fill wellsite storage by mesh size and track inventory against the stage schedule; blender operators manage chemical totes. Running short stops pumping, and trucks queue at the pad when storage is full.
process_map.unit_of_work: one pad (all proppant and chemicals received and reconciled for one multi-well pad)

evidence.note: Wellsite proppant storage and last-mile delivery (src21). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Handle screen-outs and non-productive time
process_map.description: When a stage screens out or equipment fails, the treater and supervisor decide whether to flush, call coiled tubing or swap a pump, record the lost time and agree with the customer who pays for it. Disputes over non-productive time hit field tickets.
process_map.unit_of_work: one non-productive time event (a stoppage of pumping on a pad)

evidence.note: Coil used as contingency for screen-outs (src5); delays from challenging well conditions (src7). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Rig down the frac fleet
process_map.description: After the last stage the crew flushes lines, rigs down iron, inspects and loads units and sends equipment due for maintenance to the shop. Rig-down overlaps planning for the next pad.

evidence.note: Standard fleet cycle; volume equals pads.

process_map.name: Report the frac job to the customer
process_map.description: The treater and data technician compile the treatment report from data van records, list chemicals and concentrations for the licensee's fluid disclosure and send it with job charts. Late or wrong chemical data delays the licensee's regulatory filing.
process_map.unit_of_work: one well report (treatment report and fluid disclosure data for one fractured well)

evidence.note: Fluid records submitted within 30 days of completion (src13); licensees file completion data (src10).

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Supply natural gas to dual fuel fleets
process_map.description: Coordinators order CNG or LNG deliveries for fleets with dual fuel engines, track substitution rates and fuel savings and report emissions. Gas supply interruptions push pumps back to diesel.

evidence.note: About 145,000 HHP of dual fuel capacity in 2019 (src2); Tier 4 dual gas blending fleets 2022 (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Reactivate a parked frac fleet
process_map.description: When managers decide to crew a parked fleet, the service line hires and trains a crew, recertifies equipment and adds it to the schedule. Hiring is the bottleneck; equipment can sit ready for weeks waiting for people.

evidence.note: Five to six parked crews; one crew added in Q1 2022; hiring difficulty (src1). Frequency tier C.

process_map.name: Blend and deliver bulk cement
process_map.description: Bulk plant operators blend dry cement and additives to the lab-approved recipe, sample the blend and load bulk trucks that drive to the rig. Rigs often change the call time, so blends wait or trucks rush, and a wrong blend fails on the job.
process_map.unit_of_work: one cement blend and its delivery to the wellsite

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
Cement blends and lab support (src4). Volume tier C from cement jobs.

process_map.name: Cement casing
process_map.description: A cementing crew rigs up to the rig's casing, pumps spacers and slurry to the program, displaces and bumps the plug and records returns. The job must start as soon as casing is landed, at any hour, and poor returns can mean remedial work and a regulatory issue for the licensee.
process_map.unit_of_work: one cement job (one casing string on one well)

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
16-17 units; cementing activity tracks rig count (src1); Directive 009 cementing requirements (src11). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Do remedial and abandonment cementing
process_map.description: Crews squeeze cement to repair poor primary jobs, surface casing vent flow or gas migration and set plugs for abandonment. Diagnosis is uncertain and repeat squeezes are common.

evidence.note: Remedial squeeze, plugs, vent flow and gas migration services (src4). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Report the cement job
process_map.description: The supervisor writes the cement job report with volumes, pressures, returns and plug bump and sends it with charts to the customer, who needs it for its well records. Missing returns data triggers follow-up questions.

evidence.note: Licensee must meet cement top requirements (src11). Volume equals cement jobs.

process_map.name: Plan a coiled tubing job
process_map.description: Engineers and supervisors choose the string, tools and fluids, model forces and reach for long horizontal wells, and check string fatigue before the crew leaves. Deep laterals push strings near their limits.
process_map.unit_of_work: one coiled tubing program (one well or one job)

evidence.note: Force analysis and hydraulic modelling (src5). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak on frozen ground (January to mid-March) before spring break-up

evidence.note: STEP reports seasonal weather and spring break-up effects on coiled tubing; multiplier tier C.

process_map.name: Run coiled tubing jobs
process_map.description: A 24-hour crew rigs up the injector and reel, runs in to mill frac plugs or clean out sand, circulates returns and pulls out. Stuck pipe, motor failures and slow plug drilling stretch jobs.
process_map.unit_of_work: one coiled tubing job (usually one well's plug millout or cleanout)

evidence.note: Six crews; operating days up 6% in 2022 (src1); services described (src5). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak on frozen ground before spring break-up

evidence.note: Seasonal weather and break-up effects on coiled tubing (step-2021); multiplier tier C.

process_map.name: Pump nitrogen
process_map.description: Nitrogen operators pump nitrogen for coiled tubing cleanouts, well kick-offs and purges, managing liquid nitrogen supply from gas suppliers. Supply trucks must arrive on time or the job stops.

evidence.note: Nitrogen services (src5, src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Track coiled tubing string life
process_map.description: After each job, cycles and pressures are added to the string's fatigue record; strings are cut, inspected or retired and new strings ordered. Running a string past its life risks a failure downhole.

evidence.note: Coiled tubing strings bought as raw material (src1); fatigue modelling (src5). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Report the coiled tubing job
process_map.description: The supervisor sends the customer a job record with depths, plugs milled, fluids and nitrogen pumped and any problems. Reports are written at the end of long shifts and sometimes late.

evidence.note: Standard practice; volume equals coiled tubing jobs.

process_map.name: Design fracturing treatments
process_map.description: Design engineers build the pump schedule per stage from the producer's completion design, offset results and lab data, choose fluids and proppant, and update designs when the producer changes plans. Designs feed bids, material orders and the treater's job plan.
process_map.unit_of_work: one pad design (pump schedules for all wells on a pad)

evidence.note: Engineering support and lab services (src6); subsurface integrity planning under Directive 083 is the licensee's duty with service company input (src9). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Design cement slurries and run lab tests
process_map.description: Lab technologists test the proposed blend with field water at well temperature for thickening time, strength and fluid loss, and engineers issue the cement program. Rigs give short notice, so tests run overnight and a failed test delays the job.
process_map.unit_of_work: one cement design (one casing string for one well or a repeat design for a pad)

evidence.note: Cement design software and lab support (src4); Directive 009 requirements (src11). Volume tier C: most intermediate and production jobs, few surface jobs.

process_map.name: Test fluids, chemicals and proppant
process_map.description: The lab runs sieve and crush tests on sand, checks chemical batches and tests producer water for compatibility with the fluid system. Out-of-spec sand or water forces design changes or rejected loads.
process_map.unit_of_work: one quality sample (a sand lot or railcar sample, a chemical batch or a water sample)

evidence.note: Full service fracturing lab (src6). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak and pre-season sand stockpiling (November to mid-March)

evidence.note: Estimate tied to the winter fracturing peak described in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Analyse job data
process_map.description: Data analysts and engineers compare treatment data, non-productive time and cement results across wells and write analyses for customers and for design improvement. Data sits in data van files and spreadsheets.

evidence.note: Job data streamed to engineers (src5). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Develop new chemicals and blends
process_map.description: Research chemists test new friction reducers, cement blends and lost circulation products, run field trials and release product specifications. Trials depend on customers willing to try them.

evidence.note: R&D centre (src3) and proprietary blends (src4). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Buy proppant and manage rail supply
process_map.description: Buyers release sand from term supply agreements to match pad schedules, track railcars to in-basin terminals and balance inventory across terminals and sizes. Rail delays and program changes leave sand short at one terminal and surplus at another.
process_map.unit_of_work: one proppant release (sand for one pad or terminal top-up, typically 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes)

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
1.3-1.4 million tonnes pumped a year; proppant sourced as raw material; some customers buy sand directly (src1); unit-train terminals (src21). Release count tier C.

process_map.name: Schedule sand hauling to pads
process_map.description: Logistics coordinators turn the stage schedule into hourly truck orders from terminals to pads, dispatch carriers, track load tickets and react to road bans, weather and pump schedule changes. Trucks waiting at a full pad or a fleet waiting on sand both cost money.
process_map.unit_of_work: one truckload of frac sand (about 38 tonnes on a B-train pneumatic trailer)

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews and units fully booked through January, February and the first half of March, then seasonal decline before spring break-up (src2). Multiplier tier C.
Tonnes from src1; loads tier C at about 38 tonnes per truck.

process_map.name: Buy, blend and deliver chemicals
process_map.description: Buyers order additives, the blending plant mixes and packages them, and deliveries go to pads and bases with dangerous goods documents. Long lead times on some additives and sudden design changes cause shortages.
process_map.unit_of_work: one chemical order (the additives for one pad, or a base stock top-up)

evidence.note: Chemical sales and supply chain lead times (src1). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same winter peak as the proppant and frac processes in the organisation file; the organisation file entry for this process has no surge.

process_map.name: Supply cement and additives to bulk plants
process_map.description: Buyers keep bulk plants stocked with oilwell cement and additives, ordering from cement suppliers and moving stock between plants. A plant running short cannot blend for the next rig call.

evidence.note: Oilwell cement named as a raw material (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Buy parts and materials
process_map.description: Buyers turn requisitions from shops into purchase orders for fluid ends, valves, engines and coiled tubing strings, chase suppliers and expedite urgent parts. Long lead times in 2021-2022 left units waiting on parts.
process_map.unit_of_work: one purchase order (or requisition filled by transfer)

evidence.note: Supply chain challenges and long lead times on key parts (src1). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Spring break-up maintenance and rebuild season while road bans park the fleets (April to early June)

evidence.note: Spring break-up restricts equipment moves (step_2021); the organisation file treats break-up as a maintenance surge. Multiplier is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Run warehouses and inventory
process_map.description: Warehouse staff receive goods, issue parts to work orders, cycle count and keep stock across bases. Parts taken without a transaction make the counts wrong, and shops then find a part missing when a unit is already torn down.

evidence.note: Typical transaction volume for a fleet of this size.

process_map.name: Ship dangerous goods
process_map.description: Staff classify acids and chemicals, prepare shipping documents and placards and check driver training before loads leave. Errors bring roadside fines and can stop a load at a weigh scale while the pad waits for chemicals.

evidence.note: Based on Transportation of Dangerous Goods practice for oilfield chemicals and acids; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Manage suppliers and supply contracts
process_map.description: Supply chain managers negotiate term agreements for sand, chemicals, cement, fuel and parts, review supplier performance and handle price escalations. Inflation in 2022 reopened many agreements.

evidence.note: Record inflation and supply chain challenges in 2022 (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Supply diesel to locations
process_map.description: Coordinators schedule diesel deliveries to pads and bases to keep pumps and trucks running around the clock and reconcile delivery tickets. A missed delivery shuts a fleet down.

evidence.note: About 1-2 deliveries per active fleet per day plus bases.

process_map.name: Do preventive maintenance
process_map.description: Planners issue work orders by hours and pad cycles, and technicians service engines, transmissions, power ends and fluid ends between pads or in break-up. High-pressure pumping wears parts in hours, so maintenance competes with keeping fleets working.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: road bans park the fleet and equipment comes into shops for overhaul

evidence.note: Break-up restricts equipment moves (src7); road bans during thaw (src12). Shop multiplier tier C.
Repair costs and mechanics in cost of sales; maintenance capital $30.0 million in 2022 (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Repair equipment and rebuild pumps
process_map.description: Technicians diagnose failed units, replace fluid ends, valves and seats, rebuild power ends and engines and return units to service. Parts waits and mechanic shortages decide how many pumps a fleet can field.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: road bans park the fleet and equipment comes into shops for overhaul

evidence.note: Break-up restricts equipment moves (src7); road bans during thaw (src12). Shop multiplier tier C.
Repair costs in cost of sales and parts lead times (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Inspect and certify treating iron
process_map.description: Technicians clean, inspect, thickness test and pressure test treating iron, valves and connections on a fixed cycle and tag each piece. Uncertified iron cannot go to location.

evidence.note: Industry practice for high-pressure flow iron recertification; volume estimated from fleet size.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: parked fleets send their iron in for recertification before the next season

evidence.note: Break-up reduces field activity (src1) and road bans start with the spring thaw (src6). The multiplier is tier C.

process_map.name: Build and upgrade equipment
process_map.description: Engineers and technicians upgrade pumps to dual fuel or Tier 4 engines, build or refurbish units and electrify equipment under approved capital projects. Engine and component lead times set the schedule.
process_map.unit_of_work: one unit build or upgrade (for example one frac pump converted to a Tier 4 DGB engine)

evidence.note: Tier 4 DGB fleet upgrades (three fleets, 126,000 HHP at end of 2022); growth capital $73.7 million (src1); 10 pumps converted to dual fuel in 2019 (src2). Units per month tier C.

surge.cause: Spring break-up shop window, when idle fleets free units for upgrade work

evidence.note: Author's estimate: shops schedule upgrade work into break-up, when most fleets are parked by road bans.

process_map.name: Inspect commercial vehicles
process_map.description: Mechanics perform annual commercial vehicle inspections and safety repairs on tractors, trailers and bulk trucks and keep the certificates. An expired inspection takes a unit off the road.

evidence.note: About 600 commercial vehicles inspected once a year.

process_map.name: Repair equipment on location
process_map.description: Field mechanics are called out to pads and rigs to fix pumps, engines and controls during jobs. Travel to remote leases takes hours while the crew waits.

evidence.note: Breakdown call-outs estimated at 2-6 per active fleet per week.

surge.cause: Extreme cold snaps (below about -30 C) raise engine, fuel, hydraulic and control failures on location

evidence.note: Author's estimate from WCSB winter operations; no published count of call-outs opened.

process_map.name: Sell surplus equipment
process_map.description: Equipment engineers and finance list idle or obsolete units, find buyers, often outside the WCSB, and close the sale. Prices depend on the US market.

evidence.note: About $32 million of non-core equipment and property sold in 2019, all specialised equipment sold outside Canada (src2). Count tier C.

process_map.name: Assess hazards before each job
process_map.description: Before each job or shift the supervisor leads a field level hazard assessment and safety meeting covering pressure, H2S, traffic and simultaneous operations, and records it for the customer. Short-cut assessments are a common audit finding.
process_map.unit_of_work: one field level hazard assessment (one job, or one shift on a fracturing pad)

evidence.note: Alberta OHS rules (src15); H2S training (src14). Volume tier C: per job and per frac shift. Revised 2026-11-24: owned by field operations: service-line supervisors lead the hazard assessments, with HSE advisors in support, as the ofs-05 workflow author found.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak on frozen ground

evidence.note: Tracks field activity, which peaks January to mid-March in the organisation file.

process_map.name: Report and investigate incidents
process_map.description: Workers report injuries, near misses, spills and vehicle incidents; HSE advisors investigate, assign corrective actions and notify the customer, regulators and the workers' compensation board when required. Investigations stall when crews rotate out.
process_map.unit_of_work: one incident or near miss (or one audit finding handled as a case)

evidence.note: Safety performance is a key customer criterion (src1); OHS rules (src15). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak with new and recalled crews

evidence.note: Incidents track hours worked and crew inexperience; multiplier estimated.

process_map.name: Train and certify field staff
process_map.description: Trainers run orientation, H2S Alive, first aid, driving and service-line courses, track ticket expiries and sign off competencies. Hiring waves in 2021-2022 overloaded training, and new hires could not go to location until their tickets were complete.
process_map.unit_of_work: one training enrolment (one worker completing one course or competency module)

evidence.note: H2S Alive is one day, valid three years (src14). Volume tier C.

surge.cause: Hiring wave for crew reactivation or pre-season staffing, with every new hire needing a full set of tickets

evidence.note: Adding field crews was difficult and the company competed to attract personnel (src4); multiplier estimated from four to six courses per new hire during a hiring drive.

process_map.name: Audit and inspect field safety
process_map.description: HSE advisors audit jobs, bases and shops against company rules and customer requirements and report findings. Audits rely on advisors who also handle incidents and rotate with crews, so audit plans slip when field activity peaks.

evidence.note: About three audits per advisor per month.

process_map.name: Respond to and report spills
process_map.description: When fluid, fuel or chemical is released on location, the crew contains it, the environmental specialist reports to the licensee and, where required, the regulator, and arranges cleanup. Reporting duties sit mostly with the licensee.

evidence.note: Regulator notification channels for fracturing events (src9). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Keep customer safety prequalification current
process_map.description: HSE coordinators submit safety statistics, programs, insurance and training records to ISNetworld, ComplyWorks and customer forms so the company stays approved. A lapsed grade blocks work for that customer.

evidence.note: Common practice for WCSB contractors serving many producers.

process_map.name: Manage driver hours and fatigue
process_map.description: Coordinators audit driver logs, manage oil well service vehicle permits and flag drivers near limits so schedules change. Long moves after 12-hour shifts are the main risk.

evidence.note: Permit rules: three 24-hour off-duty periods in any 24 days, 72 hours off after permit driving (src18). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Recruit and hire field staff
process_map.description: Recruiters post jobs, screen for Class 1 licences and tickets, interview with supervisors, check references and drug and alcohol tests, and make offers. Competition for experienced operators made hiring the bottleneck to adding crews.
process_map.unit_of_work: one hire (one field employee recruited and cleared to start)

surge.cause: Crew reactivation hiring drive when a parked fleet or crew is restarted

evidence.note: One frac crew and one coiled tubing crew added in Q1 2022 (src1); STEP grew its Canadian workforce 15% in 2022 (src8). Multiplier tier C.
Significant challenges attracting and retaining qualified personnel (src1). Hires per month tier C (about 25-35% annual turnover plus growth).

process_map.name: Onboard new employees
process_map.description: HR coordinators set up employee records, benefits, rotations and system access and book orientation and safety courses. Missing paperwork delays first pay and system access, and new field hires often start on short notice.

evidence.note: Same volume as hires.

process_map.name: Lay off and recall staff
process_map.description: When activity drops, managers choose who to lay off, HR issues notices and records, and when work returns staff are recalled. The 2020 downturn and 2021-2022 recovery made this a large process.

evidence.note: Wage subsidy (CEWS) offset $10.2 million of 2021 personnel costs (src1), reflecting the 2020-2021 downturn. Counts tier C.

process_map.name: Set pay and benefits
process_map.description: Compensation specialists maintain field pay levels, day rates, job bonuses and benefits and set annual increases within the budget. Wage cuts in 2020 and restorations in 2022 changed every table.

evidence.note: Wages increased and benefits reinstated in 2022 (src8). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Manage field progression
process_map.description: Supervisors assess operators against level requirements, HR records promotions and pay changes. Progression keeps people from leaving for competitors, but sign-offs wait until supervisor and worker are on the same rotation.

evidence.note: Field level systems common in pressure pumping.

process_map.name: Turn field tickets into invoices
process_map.description: Billing specialists match signed field tickets to the price book, build the invoice in the ERP and submit it through the customer's e-invoicing network, then rework rejections. Coding rules differ by customer and rejected invoices wait weeks.
process_map.unit_of_work: one customer invoice (one job, one well or one pad, made of one or more field tickets)

surge.cause: Year-end and Q1 invoice wave as producers close capital programs and winter work peaks

evidence.note: December program completions (src2 notes typical December declines as customers finish programs) followed by the winter peak.
Job count equals invoices (src1). Steps tier C.

process_map.name: Collect customer payments
process_map.description: Credit analysts apply payments, follow up overdue and disputed invoices with producers and set credit limits. One customer held 35-40% of receivables, so its payment timing moves cash.
process_map.unit_of_work: one collection follow-up (an overdue, short-paid or disputed invoice taken up by the credit team)

evidence.note: One customer 35% of receivables in 2021 and 40% in 2022 (src1). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Pay suppliers and carriers
process_map.description: AP clerks match supplier and carrier invoices to purchase orders, receipts and load tickets, resolve differences with buyers and coordinators and run payments. Thousands of sand haul tickets make matching heavy.

surge.cause: Year-end and Q1 invoice wave as producers close capital programs and winter work peaks

evidence.note: December program completions (src2 notes typical December declines as customers finish programs) followed by the winter peak.
Direct costs of $345-508 million a year are mostly supplier spend (src1). Invoice count tier C.

process_map.name: Run payroll
process_map.description: Payroll specialists collect field time, day rates and job bonuses, process biweekly pay for about 1,350 employees, remit deductions and post the ledger. Late or wrong field time causes off-cycle corrections.

evidence.note: Volume from ofs-fin-payroll-processing (2026-11-24): Biweekly pay for field and office staff is the common pattern at Canadian service companies; 26 runs a year gives 2.17 a month, matching the organisation file's 2-2.2-3.

surge.cause: Spring break-up layoffs and summer recall, adding terminations, ROEs and rehires to the runs

evidence.note: The number of runs does not change during break-up (multiplier 1.0); the work inside each run rises by an estimated 20-40% because of terminations, ROEs and recalls. Recorded here so a simulation can raise per-run effort, not run counts.

process_map.name: Close the books monthly
process_map.description: Accountants accrue unbilled work and uninvoiced costs, reconcile accounts and inventory and produce monthly results by service line. Field tickets not yet signed make revenue accruals uncertain.

evidence.note: Standard monthly close.

surge.cause: Quarter-end and year-end close for public reporting and the external auditor

evidence.note: Listed issuers file interim statements each quarter; the extra effort per quarter-end close (30-100% more accountant hours) is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare quarterly and annual disclosure
process_map.description: Finance prepares financial statements, MD&A, the annual information form and press releases, works with the auditor and the board and files them publicly. Deadlines are fixed by securities rules.

evidence.note: Annual MD&A and statements published (src1).

process_map.name: Budget and forecast
process_map.description: Analysts build the annual budget and quarterly forecasts by service line from customer programs, crew plans and cost inflation. Forecasts change with commodity prices and customer budgets, so the plan is often redone within weeks.

evidence.note: Standard annual budget with quarterly reforecasts.

process_map.name: Plan and approve capital spending
process_map.description: Finance and operations rank capital requests for upgrades, reactivations and maintenance capital, and executives or the board approve them. Return hurdles decide which fleets get upgraded.

evidence.note: Capital spending $33.2 million (2019), $53.9 million (2021), $103.6 million (2022); return hurdle discipline (src2). Request count tier C.

process_map.name: Claim wage and rent subsidies
process_map.description: In 2020 and 2021 finance and payroll prepared Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy and rent subsidy claims each period from payroll and revenue data. Claims needed careful eligibility calculations and audit files.

evidence.note: CEWS reduced 2021 personnel costs by $10.2 million and CERS $0.8 million (src1). None in 2019 or 2022.

process_map.name: Manage cash and the credit facility
process_map.description: Treasury forecasts cash, draws or repays the revolving facility, monitors covenants and manages share buybacks and dividends approved by the board. Customer payment timing, with one customer holding up to 40% of receivables, drives the forecast.

evidence.note: Unused committed facilities $94.6-124.6 million; NCIB and dividend (src1).

process_map.name: Run the IT service desk
process_map.description: Support technicians handle access requests, device issues and application problems from bases, shops and field crews, escalating system issues to analysts. Field users call at all hours.

evidence.note: About 0.4 tickets per employee per month.

process_map.name: Support field connectivity and data vans
process_map.description: Network specialists keep satellite and cellular links, data van computers and tablet ticketing working on remote pads. A data van outage stops a frac job.

evidence.note: Estimated from seven fleets and 30-plus field units.

process_map.name: Support the ERP and business applications
process_map.description: ERP analysts configure price books, maintenance, procurement and billing, apply vendor releases and fix interface errors between field ticketing, ERP and customer e-invoicing. Interface failures hold invoices until fixed.

evidence.note: Typical change volume for a mid-size ERP.

process_map.name: Review contracts
process_map.description: Legal counsel reviews customer master service agreements and supplier contracts, focusing on indemnities, insurance, liability caps and escalation, and returns markups. Producer forms and urgent awards compress review time.

evidence.note: Estimated from tender and supplier contract volumes.

process_map.name: Manage insurance and claims
process_map.description: The risk manager renews the insurance program, issues certificates for customers and portals and manages equipment, vehicle and liability claims. Customers ask for certificates with every new contract.

evidence.note: Insured fire event and equipment replacement (src2). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Track regulatory changes
process_map.description: Regulatory advisors watch AER, BC, OHS and transport rule changes, assess their effect on field work and brief operations, HSE and engineering. Most rules bind the licensee, so changes also reach the company through customer procedures.

evidence.note: Directive editions change regularly (src9-src11). Volume tier C.

process_map.name: Plan strategy and govern with the board
process_map.description: Executives set fleet, market and capital strategy, prepare board materials and carry out board decisions on capital, dividends and buybacks. Plans hinge on producer spending and pipeline capacity, which the company cannot control.

evidence.note: Return of capital strategy and fleet upgrade program (src1).

process_map.name: Manage enterprise risk
process_map.description: Executives and the general counsel review the risk register: customer concentration, labour shortage, cost inflation, safety and regulation, and agree mitigations. Each risk has an owner who reports progress to the board each quarter.

evidence.note: Risks listed in src1: personnel shortage, cost escalation, customer dependence, safety.

process_map.name: Review operating performance
process_map.description: The COO and service line directors review utilization, pricing, safety and margins each month and decide to activate, park or move crews. Decisions lag the market because the data arrives after the month-end close.

evidence.note: Crew activation and utilization decisions (src1).

assumptions: The organisation is a composite modelled mainly on Trican Well Service, the largest Canadian pressure pumper, using its 2019 and 2022 public results; STEP Energy Services' Canadian segment is used for workforce size and coiled tubing activity. Figures are averages over 2019-2022 unless a year is named; 2020 was a severe downturn (lower activity, layoffs, wage subsidy) and is covered by the low ends of ranges.

Trican also has a base in Estevan, Saskatchewan and a cementing and acidizing business beyond the three main lines; the file keeps to Alberta and northeast BC and treats acidizing and nitrogen as part of coiled tubing.

Headcount was first set at 1,350 (tier C) and revised on 2026-11-24 to 1,387 to cover the work the workflows record. Trican reported 1,124 full and part time employees at the end of 2022 (src-trican-aif23), so the file sits above the company it is modelled on; crew sizes, contracted trucking or workflow step times may explain the gap. Role headcounts are sized from crew counts at three rotating shift crews per 24-hour frac or coiled tubing crew.

Loaded cost per hour = base wage x 1.35 (benefits, WCB premiums, CPP/EI, overtime premium on rotation, overhead). Field wages come from the 2023 Alberta Wage and Salary Survey reduced about 8% to 2019-2022 levels; office and executive costs are estimates.

Job volumes by service line (about 50 frac wells, 400 cement jobs and 140 coiled tubing and nitrogen jobs a month) are tier C splits of the tier A annual job totals, using revenue shares and crew counts. A job is roughly one invoice, as the company defines it.
Proppant is shown as bought and delivered by the company; some customers buy sand directly (src1), which reduces the company's procurement volume but not its on-site handling.

Regulatory filings on fracturing (Directive 083 notifications, Directive 059 data, FracFocus disclosure) and cementing compliance (Directive 009) are the licensee's legal duties; the company supplies the data and follows customer procedures. Regulator web pages were opened in their current editions; the same directives were in force during 2019-2022 in earlier editions.

Spring break-up is described as a surge on the maintenance processes and as a restart surge on mobilization; the drop in field volume during break-up is covered by the low end of field process volumes.
Systems are generic for the period (ERP with plant maintenance, tablet field ticketing, customer e-invoicing networks, prequalification portals); vendor names are illustrative where given.
